properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RC4 API surface of crypto-js@3.1.9-1, a transitive dependency (via @cityofzion/neon-js-legacy) that ships in the production bundle. No application call site found — the image ships the algorithm whether or not this app invokes it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile declaration of hash.js 1.1.7 (with ^1.0.0/^1.0.3 ranges), pulled in transitively via elliptic@6.4.1 which uses it for SHA-1/SHA-256 message hashing in ECDSA. The build ships the SHA-1 and SHA-2 families through this entry; no direct call site in the app's own code — it is consumed inside the bundled crypto dependencies of the NEO wallet's chain libraries.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js is locked at four versions (3.1.9-1, 4.0.0, 4.1.1 and 4.2.0); version 3.1.9-1 is the classic wallet-era release that the @cityofzion neon libraries depend on. The package exports MD5 alongside AES, so the bundled build can produce MD5 digests. Dependency inventory entry — presence in the shipped bundle is the fact recorded here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 ships inside every locked crypto-js version (3.1.9-1 through 4.2.0); the old 3.1.9-1 release used by the NEO chain libraries makes it available at runtime. Dependency inventory entry for the shipped bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 support in elliptic (transitive dependency resolved in yarn.lock), shipped in the bundle. No application call site found; the wallet's own chain (NEO) uses secp256r1, so secp256k1 arrives purely as library surface via the neon-js/ecc dependency tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@0.10.0 resolved in yarn.lock — a transitive dependency (not imported directly by app code) that ships RSA key generation, PKCS#1 encryption/signing, and X.509/ASN.1 tooling in the bundle. Complements the separate node-forge library object.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile declaration of @noble/curves 1.0.0, pulled in by the @cityofzion neo3 blockchain-service/neon-js stack. secp256k1 support ships in the bundle through this entry even where the wallet itself addresses NEO accounts on secp256r1; the Bitcoin-style curve is available to every bundled consumer.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519/EdDSA support in @noble/curves@1.0.0 (transitive dependency via the neon-js/WalletConnect ecosystem), shipped in the bundle. Quantum-vulnerable under Shor; no direct application import found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile declaration of elliptic 6.4.1 (the old, pre-audited line — elliptic 6.4.1 is the version with the known invalid-curve/twist security issues fixed in 6.5.4). It ships the ECDSA implementation used by the wallet's EC crypto stack; note 6.5.4 is also locked for other consumers. The bundled build can run ECDSA through this entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: First-party split-key wallet feature: joinWIFKeys() derives one private key from two user-supplied WIF halves by adding them modulo the secp256r1 group order. secp256r1 is NEO's signature curve; the derived key holds classical ECDSA funds — retroactively breakable under Shor, but the curve is fixed by the NEO protocol, so this is observable here, replaceable only by the chain's protocol governance.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256r1 (P-256) is the curve NEO N3 accounts actually use, so this locked implementation is the one the wallet's account key handling reaches at runtime; it arrives via the @cityofzion noble-curve dependencies. Dependency inventory entry recording that P-256 ships in the bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile declaration of elliptic 6.4.1. elliptic's ec.keyFromPublic/ec.derive path implements ECDH key agreement over secp256k1/P-256; the bundled build ships that capability via the wallet's chain libraries (elliptic is also locked at 6.5.4 for other consumers).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile declaration of tweetnacl 0.14.x — the NaCl reference port exposing crypto_scalarmult (X25519) via nacl.box.keyPair/nacl.scalarMult. Pulled in transitively by the wallet-connect/relay stack of this NEO wallet; the X25519 primitive ships in the bundle through this entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The wallet's NEP-2/NEP-6 key-encryption KDF parameters: cost N=2^14, r=8, p=8, dkLen=64 — the protocol-mandated NEP-2 values, consumed by neon-js wallet.encrypt/decrypt for every encrypted private key the app stores. N=2^14 sits below OWASP's current scrypt recommendation (2^17) but is fixed by the NEP-2 standard, so not unilaterally changeable. The flow-typed stubs and yarn.lock site document the js-scrypt library surface shipped alongside.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 API surface of crypto-js@3.1.9-1 (transitive dependency via @cityofzion/neon-js-legacy) shipped in the bundle. The app itself derives keys with scrypt via neon-js (NEP-2), not crypto-js PBKDF2; recorded as available library surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES API surface of crypto-js@3.1.9-1 (transitive dependency via @cityofzion/neon-js-legacy) shipped in the bundle. The application itself does not call crypto-js AES directly; recorded as available library surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Release-integrity governance artifact: the build pipeline computes SHA-256 over release binaries so users can verify downloads. SHA-256 is Grover-halved but not broken — appropriate for artifact integrity.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 in @noble/hashes@1.3.0 — transitive dependency (via the neon-js/WalletConnect ecosystem) shipped in the bundle. Grover-halved but not broken; no direct app import found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 in @noble/hashes@1.3.0 — transitive dependency shipped in the bundle. BLAKE3 is a modern hash with no known weakness (quantum-halved like all hashes); library surface, no app call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile declaration of @noble/hashes 1.3.0, pulled in by the @cityofzion blockchain-service/neon-js stack. Ships keccak/SHA-3 in the bundle; no direct call site in the app's own sources — the consumers are the bundled chain libraries.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile declaration of tweetnacl 0.14.x. NaCl's authenticated encryption (secretbox/box) is exactly XSalsa20-Poly1305 and is quantum-resistant in the symmetric sense; it is the AE primitive the wallet-connect/NaCl consumers in this bundle reach. Dependency inventory entry.

components.name: Node.js tls sessions on default settings (Node.js version unknown)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The wallet app's entire RPC/API transport: axios HTTPS calls to dora.coz.io (balances), CoinMarketCap-style price APIs, raw.githubusercontent.com (phishing blacklist), and NEO RPC nodes, on Node/Electron DEFAULT TLS settings (no cipher/group pinning anywhere in the tree). Runtime electron@19.0.8 (devDependencies) bundles Node 16.x — predates any post-quantum key-exchange default (X25519MLKEM768 ships in Node 24.5+), so every session negotiates classical ECDHE groups: harvest-now-decrypt-later ex

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile declaration of selfsigned 1.10.x, pulled in by webpack-dev-server to mint the throwaway HTTPS certificate for the dev server. It generates self-signed X.509 certs (via node-forge) for local development — never shipped to end users, but part of the build toolchain's crypto posture. Changeable here: a dev-only dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile declaration of node-forge 0.10.x — the X.509/PKI toolkit (certificate creation, RSA, TLS in pure JS). Pulled in transitively via selfsigned/webpack-dev-server for the dev-server certificate; the bundle's toolchain ships X.509 handling through this entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile declaration of the deprecated npm "crypto" shim (v1.0.1), pulled in transitively by the WalletConnect-era stack. Whatever resolves through this stub ends at Node's built-in OpenSSL-backed crypto module, so the effective provider is the Node/OpenSSL runtime the Electron build embeds (Electron 19 → OpenSSL 1.1.1 line). Recorded as the OpenSSL-backed provider entry in the dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 in yarn.lock — ships XSalsa20-Poly1305 AEAD (secretbox), Ed25519 signatures and X25519 key agreement (crypto_box), all quantum-vulnerable except the AEAD's symmetric core. Transitive dependency of the neon-js/WalletConnect tree; dependency inventory entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@2.0.4 in yarn.lock — pure-JS scrypt KDF implementation, the same primitive neon-js uses for NEP-2 key encryption. Transitive dependency; inventory entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js@2.4.11 in yarn.lock — pure-JS SHA-1/SHA-2 family (SHA-1 is collision-broken classically). Transitive dependency of the neon-js/crypto-js ecosystem; inventory entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: md5@2.3.0 npm package in yarn.lock — a standalone MD5 implementation arriving as a transitive dependency. MD5 is collision-broken independently of quantum computing; shipped in the bundle whether or not this app calls it. Dependency inventory entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile declaration of elliptic 6.4.1 — the elliptic-curve crypto library (ECDSA, ECDH over secp256k1/secp256r1) used by the NEO chain libraries in this wallet. Note both 6.4.1 and 6.5.4 are locked; 6.4.1 predates the 2020 invalid-curve fixes, which matters for any consumer pinned to it. Dependency inventory entry for the shipped bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile declaration of the deprecated npm "crypto" shim package 1.0.1, pulled in transitively by the WalletConnect-era stack. The dependency ships in the lockfile; at runtime it resolves to Node's built-in OpenSSL-backed crypto module (see the twin ALG entry for the provider view). Recorded as-is: this is what the build declares.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes@1.3.0 in yarn.lock — hash library (SHA-2, SHA-3, BLAKE3, RIPEMD, Keccak) pulled in via the neon-js/WalletConnect ecosystem. The SHA-256/BLAKE3 algorithm facets are confirmed under their own objects; this is the library entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: selfsigned@1.10.14 in yarn.lock — generates self-signed X.509 certificates (RSA/ECDSA keys via node-forge) at runtime. Typically used by dev-server https; shipped as a resolved dependency. Its output certs use classical signatures (Shor-vulnerable); also complements the X.509 self-signed algorithm object.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 in yarn.lock — hash framework (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-2, RIPEMD) transitive dependency of elliptic. Dependency inventory entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile declaration of @noble/curves 1.0.0 — the modern audited EC library providing secp256k1, P-256, ed25519, X25519 and friends to the @cityofzion neo3 stack in this wallet. Dependency inventory entry: these curves ship in the bundle through this entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile declaration of the pbkdf2 npm package (^3.0.3) — a browserify port of Node's pbkdf2, reachable from crypto-browserify (a direct dependency in package.json) and the wallet's key-derivation paths. The PBKDF2 capability ships in the bundle; iteration-count decisions are made by consumers, which the shard-1 PBKDF2 objects cover.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile declaration of node-forge 0.10.x — pure-JS TLS/PKI (X.509 certs, RSA, PKCS). Pulled in transitively via selfsigned/webpack-dev-server for the dev-server HTTPS cert; ships in the build toolchain. Dependency inventory entry.
